coder_prompt: You are an expert Rust engineer. Write one complete, self-contained Rust source file that satisfies the task, using only the standard library. Respond with the whole file in a single ```rust fenced code block and nothing else. Include an empty `fn main() {}` (the file is compiled as a program).
lessons: Translate requirements into explicit ordered validation, parsing, and state-transition phases; define error precedence, invariants, and boundary cases before choosing an algorithm.
Validate all required input before mutation or output; preserve original indices, offsets, metadata, and distinctions that affect equality or errors.
Track positions and state explicitly across transformations, chunks, and boundaries; preserve source offsets, token boundaries, and UTF-8 scalar boundaries.
Model operations as ordered phases, applying admission, expiry, validation, and mutation exactly when specified; commit only completed work and preserve failed items.
Use checked arithmetic at each required operation or prefix; define bounds, rounding stages, and overflow precedence explicitly.
Use complete comparators and explicit tie-breaks; never rely on incidental container order.
Separate scanning and parsing from output construction; track source and transformed positions independently, and emit only after required validation succeeds.
Verify every observable result, including logs and counters, and test shared behavior, error precedence, and boundary cases across public operations.
